whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Communications Cloud Accredited Professional exam?

personas.label: Telecom delivery teams
personas.description: You implement Communications Cloud for mobile, broadband, or media providers and want to validate your industry solution skills.

personas.label: Telecom consultants and admins
personas.description: You configure product offers, quoting, or order processing for communications projects.

personas.label: Salesforce professionals entering telecom
personas.description: You know core Salesforce and want to apply it to communications service provider workflows.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Communications Cloud Accredited Professional exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers telecom-specific catalog, quoting, and order processes. Learn how Communications Cloud handles products and offers, validates a customer’s cart, and fulfills service changes.
bullets: 55 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
56% to pass, which is 31 correct answers out of 55.
Industry tools: Review Enterprise Product Catalog, Industries CPQ, Industries Order Management, and OmniStudio.
Telecom service changes: Be able to follow move, add, change, and disconnect requests, along with the customer’s contracts and assets.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice creating an offer in the product catalog and following an order through decomposition and fulfillment. Aim for 75% or more on practice questions and explain why each tool fits the task.

examFormat.heading: Communications Cloud Accredited Professional exam format
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Questions focus on common communications provider workflows.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe a telecom task, such as packaging broadband with a router, pricing a service, or changing a customer’s existing plan. Choose the catalog feature, rule, or order capability that handles it.
bestWayToPass: Learn the catalog parts: Understand products, attributes, offers, bundles, promotions, and price lists.
Know the cart rules: Eligibility determines who can buy an offer; compatibility prevents invalid combinations; context rules use customer or location details.
Trace an order: Learn how Industries Order Management decomposes an order and orchestrates the steps needed to fulfill it.
Review OmniStudio: Know what OmniScripts, FlexCards, Integration Procedures, and Data Mappers do.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you set up Communications Cloud for telecom and media providers: the product catalog, quoting, ordering and fulfilment, contracts and assets, and the OmniStudio tools. The exam is 55 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 56% pass mark, weighted towards Planning and Design (60%) and Discovery (24%).

keyConcepts.h2: Communications Cloud AP: core exam concepts

blocks.heading: Product Catalog & Offer Management
blocks.body: The **Enterprise Product Catalog (EPC)** stores the products and offers a provider sells. A **product** describes a service or device; its **attributes** capture choices such as speed or color. An **offer** is what a customer can buy and may combine several products into a **bundle**, such as broadband and TV. **Promotions** apply limited-time discounts, while **price lists** hold prices that may vary by market or channel. Reusable products let a change, such as replacing a router model, carry through to every offer that uses it.

blocks.heading: Industries CPQ for Telecom
blocks.body: **Industries CPQ** provides a cart where an agent or customer selects offers, chooses attributes, and sees the price. Rules keep choices valid. **Eligibility rules** decide whether a customer can buy an offer, perhaps based on service location. **Compatibility rules** prevent combinations that cannot work together, such as two broadband plans on one line. **Context rules** use customer or location information to change what appears. The cart can support agent workflows and **Digital Commerce** channels through APIs.

blocks.heading: Order Management & Orchestration
blocks.body: When a customer submits an order, **Industries Order Management** uses **decomposition** to break the commercial request into the technical work needed to deliver it. An **orchestration plan** runs the work in the required sequence. For example, the plan may reserve a phone number, ship a router, and then activate a line, while communicating with external systems. If a task fails, the plan can retry, wait, or alert an operator. The customer sees one order even when several back-office tasks are required.

blocks.heading: Contract & Subscription Lifecycle
blocks.body: After fulfillment, the customer’s services are recorded as **assets** on the account. Later service requests often use **MACD**: move, add, change, or disconnect. Upgrading a broadband speed changes an existing asset rather than starting an unrelated service. **Contracts** record terms such as commitment length and early termination fees, and may be renewed. Accurate assets give future service changes a reliable starting point.

blocks.heading: Partner Ecosystem & Channel Management
blocks.body: Communications providers may sell through retail shops, partners, and online channels. An Experience Cloud site can give partners sales tools that use the same catalog and cart as internal agents, with channel-specific prices or offers. **OmniStudio** supports many guided experiences: **OmniScripts** guide users through steps, **FlexCards** summarize customer information, **Integration Procedures** gather data from systems, and **Data Mappers** read, transform, and save records.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Communications Cloud AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: For each telecom scenario, identify whether the task belongs to the catalog, quoting cart, order fulfillment, or service assets. Then choose the feature that owns that part of the workflow.

blocks.heading: Telecom Customer and Asset Data
blocks.body: Know how customer, billing, and service accounts can represent different parts of a relationship. Service assets show which products and services the customer currently has.

blocks.heading: Offer Rules in Industries CPQ
blocks.body: Use eligibility to decide whether a customer can buy an offer and compatibility to block combinations that do not work together. If an offer is missing, check eligibility and context.

blocks.heading: Order Decomposition and Fulfillment
blocks.body: Decomposition turns the customer’s commercial order into technical work. Orchestration plans run the fulfillment steps and handle failures.

blocks.heading: Agent Views with OmniStudio
blocks.body: FlexCards summarize services, bills, and open orders for an agent. Use OmniScripts for guided tasks and Integration Procedures for server-side calls across systems.

blocks.heading: OmniStudio Data Handling
blocks.body: Data Mappers read, transform, and save data for OmniStudio flows. Learn which data operation is needed at each point in a guided process.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Communications Cloud:

sampleQuestions.question: A provider wants one offer that includes broadband, a router, and TV at a package price. How should it model the offer?
options: Create one price list entry for a single product
Create a bundle offer from the three products
Put the three products on a contract without an offer
sampleQuestions.explanation: A bundle lets the provider sell several products together as one offer with a package price.
whyWrong: A price list stores prices; it does not combine three products into one customer offer.
A contract records customer terms, but it does not replace the offer and bundle structure.
Separate orders would not present the requested single package to the customer.

sampleQuestions.question: A fiber plan should be available only at addresses where fiber service is ready. Which rule should control access to the offer?
options: A rule that blocks incompatible products from being ordered together
A price list that sets the amount charged for the offer
An eligibility rule for the offer
A promotion that applies a temporary discount to the offer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Eligibility rules decide whether a customer can see or select an offer based on factors such as service location.
whyWrong: Compatibility rules prevent invalid combinations, rather than deciding whether a customer qualifies for one offer.
A price list sets prices; it does not check service availability.
A promotion changes an offer or price for a period but does not determine network eligibility.

sampleQuestions.question: Customers must not add two broadband plans to the same service line. What should prevent that combination?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A compatibility rule blocks combinations that cannot be used together in the cart.
whyWrong: Data Mappers handle data operations in OmniStudio, not cart validation.
FlexCards display information and actions; they do not validate product combinations.
Eligibility determines whether an offer is available, not whether it conflicts with another selected offer.

sampleQuestions.question: A broadband order requires a port reservation, router shipment, and line activation. What feature breaks the customer order into this technical work?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order Management decomposition turns the commercial request into the technical orders or tasks needed for fulfillment.
whyWrong: A promotion changes price or offer terms; it does not split an order for delivery.
A price list stores product prices and does not create technical fulfillment work.
Eligibility decides whether an offer can be purchased, not how it is fulfilled.

sampleQuestions.question: After decomposition, what runs fulfillment tasks in sequence and can call external systems?
sampleQuestions.explanation: An orchestration plan coordinates fulfillment steps, dependencies, and interactions with other systems.
whyWrong: Eligibility rules determine offer access before purchase.
A contract records terms but does not coordinate fulfillment tasks.
A FlexCard presents information in a user interface.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer asks to raise an existing broadband service from 100 Mbps to 500 Mbps. How should the request be recorded?
options: As a second, unrelated broadband order
By changing the catalog price list
As a change order for the existing asset
By deleting the current asset before placing a new order
sampleQuestions.explanation: An upgrade is a change to the customer’s existing asset, preserving the service history and avoiding duplicate services.
whyWrong: A new unrelated order may create a second service instead of changing the existing one.
The price list controls prices, not changes to a customer’s installed service.
Deleting the asset would remove useful history and is not the right way to manage a service change.

sampleQuestions.question: An agent must follow a guided set of steps to move a customer’s service to a new address. Which tool fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScripts guide users through a multi-step task such as a service move.
whyWrong: Compatibility rules validate product combinations in a cart.
Price lists hold product prices, not agent workflow steps.
Data Mappers move and transform data; they do not guide the user through the process.

sampleQuestions.question: An agent needs a compact view of a customer’s services, latest bill, and open orders. What should the page use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A FlexCard presents key customer details and actions in a compact view.
whyWrong: An orchestration plan coordinates order fulfillment steps.
Promotions define limited-time offer or price changes.
Decomposition breaks an order into work; it does not display the customer summary.

sampleQuestions.question: A screen must gather information from billing, network inventory, and Salesforce in one server-side operation. What should it use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Integration Procedure can run multiple data operations on the server and return the results to the screen.
whyWrong: A FlexCard displays information, but by itself it does not perform all the needed cross-system data calls.
A promotion defines an offer or discount, not an integration flow.
A price list holds product prices and does not retrieve billing or network data.

sampleQuestions.question: A new router replaces an older model used in 20 offers. Why build those offers from reusable products?
options: Customers must place every order again
The team must edit every offer separately
All offers stop working when the router changes
One product update can flow to every offer that uses it
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reusable catalog products reduce repeated changes because offers can use the updated product definition.
whyWrong: Changing a product definition does not require customers to reorder existing services.
Reusable products reduce the need to edit each offer independently.
A product update does not automatically disable offers that reference it.

sampleQuestions.question: A provider wants a 20% discount for new mobile customers for three months. What should represent the limited-time discount?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A promotion applies a discount or other offer change for a defined period or customer group.
whyWrong: A new product would represent a different service or device, not a temporary discount.
Compatibility rules block invalid combinations rather than apply discounts.
Orchestration plans coordinate fulfillment steps after an order is placed.

sampleQuestions.question: Why must customer service assets stay accurate?
options: Assets determine which price list appears in the catalog
Assets are used only for reports
Future moves, changes, and disconnects start from the current assets
sampleQuestions.explanation: MACD requests act on existing service assets. If those records are wrong, later changes may also be wrong.
whyWrong: Website appearance is controlled through design and content settings.
Price lists define prices; service assets do not set catalog pricing.
Assets support service operations, not reporting alone.

sampleQuestions.question: A retail partner should use the same product catalog as internal agents but have different prices. What should the provider configure?
options: Copy the entire catalog for the partner
Change prices by hand on each order
Create a separate Salesforce org for the partner
sampleQuestions.explanation: A separate price list can provide channel-specific prices while the partner continues to use the shared catalog.
whyWrong: Duplicating the catalog adds maintenance and risks differences in product definitions.
Manual order changes are inconsistent and difficult to govern.
A separate org is not needed just to set different channel prices.

sampleQuestions.question: A fulfillment step fails because the network activation system is unavailable. What should the orchestration plan do?
options: Retry or pause the step and notify an operator
Mark the order complete even though activation failed
sampleQuestions.explanation: The plan can retry, wait, or raise an alert so the failed step can resume when the external system is available.
whyWrong: Completing the order despite failed activation would leave service undelivered.
Deleting the order loses the customer request and its progress.
A duplicate order can cause conflicting fulfillment work.

sampleQuestions.question: An OmniScript needs to read Salesforce data, transform it, and save the result. Which OmniStudio tool is designed for that?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Mappers read, transform, and write data for OmniStudio workflows.
whyWrong: Promotions manage offers and discounts rather than data mapping.
Price lists define product pricing and do not transform Salesforce records.
FlexCards display information and actions; they do not perform the data transformation.
